claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 9110 defines each method against 'the target resource' with no URL-shape rule: 9.3.3 "The POST method requests that the target resource process the representation enclosed in the request according to the resource's own specific semantics." claim_verdicts.evidence: Kind opinion, framed in-text as convention ("Under this convention, such an action segment fits when ..."); consistent with repo's PATCH /api/v1/orders/{id}/cancel. Opened: refs/rfc/rfc9110.txt, refs aspnetcore routing.md (fundamentals + mvc), stage-1 controllers, OrderService.cs, Program.cs, up.sh, Caddyfile, seed.sql.

issues.quote: `login` is a verb, same as `cancel` — and that's fine for the same reason: no order, product, or other thing is being named here
issues.text: The stated reason for `cancel` (§4, §5) is that it follows an existing item URL as a named action; the reason for `login` is that no resource noun exists to be displaced. "For the same reason" asserts an equivalence the lesson's own text contradicts.
issues.fix: Replace "and that's fine for the same reason:" with "but it is fine for a different reason:".

issues.quote: `/api/v1/orders`, which creates an order, and `/api/v1/orders/1`, which reads one back by id.
issues.text: The situation says a URL "creates" and a URL "reads" — the exact idea the lesson later tells me is wrong (the method does that). On a first read it plants the view I'm about to unlearn.
issues.fix: Write "`POST /api/v1/orders`, which creates an order, and `GET /api/v1/orders/1`, which reads one back by id".

issues.quote: Under this convention, such an action segment fits when the server carries out a named action with its own rules — steps beyond storing what the client sent, like the notification Đơn Hàng sends when an order is cancelled.
issues.text: I read this paragraph twice: verb never replaces the noun, when an action segment fits, when a plain PATCH is enough, and the cancelOrder verdict are packed into four long sentences.
issues.fix: Split the paragraph after its first sentence so "when an action segment fits" and "when a plain PATCH is enough" form their own short paragraph.

issues.quote: `login` is a verb, same as `cancel` — and that's fine for the same reason: no order, product, or other thing is being named here, so no noun is being pushed aside for it.
issues.text: "For the same reason" trips me: cancel was fine because it follows an existing item URL; login is fine because there is no noun to push aside. Two different reasons, so I re-read to check whether I misunderstood cancel.
issues.fix: Replace "and that's fine for the same reason:" with "but it is fine for a different reason:".

issues.quote: "The `v1` in `/api/v1/orders` refers to the version of each individual order, not this whole set of endpoints."
issues.text: I would not have guessed per-order versions; I simply didn't know what `v1` meant. The correction brings in an idea (a version for a whole set of endpoints) the lesson never uses for its main point.
issues.fix: Replace with a misconception about the main idea, e.g. "`PATCH /api/v1/orders/{id}/cancel` breaks the rule because `cancel` is a verb in the URL", and correct it.

issues.quote: This matches Core concepts exactly: a collection URL and an item URL are two different resources, not two spellings of one.
issues.text: I go back to Core concepts and don't find "two different resources, not two spellings"; that sentence is in How it works and summary line 2. The pointer sends me to the wrong section.
issues.fix: Change "This matches Core concepts exactly" to "This matches How it works".

issues.quote: the part before `/cancel` — the order's own item URL — is ____.
issues.text: The blank is literally the text before `/cancel` in the same sentence, so I can copy it without understanding item URLs at all.
issues.fix: Ask instead for the item URL of the order that `PATCH /api/v1/orders/7/cancel` acts on, with `/api/v1/orders/7` as the answer.

issues.quote: the noun belongs in the path and the action stays out of it.
issues.text: The lesson taught that an action may stay in the path as its own segment after the item URL (`.../cancel`). "The action stays out of it" contradicts that, and I can't tell where a search would go. Also b, c, d each invent a "never"/version rule, so a wins by elimination.
issues.fix: Replace "and the action stays out of it" with "and the verb must not stand in for that noun".

issues.quote: `.../cancel` changes an order's status with PATCH, not POST — the same method fits `reopen`
issues.text: The lesson never says which method a named action segment should use; it only shows cancel with PATCH. Prereq says POST has the server process what you send, which is how I'd read "reopen with rules", so this adds a rule I can't trace to the text.
issues.fix: Drop "— the same method fits `reopen`" from explanation d, keeping only that the method question does not excuse the verb in the URL.
